newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Clinton elated by warmth of Australian reception.
newsitem.headline: Clinton elated by warmth of Australian reception.

text.p: Buoyed by his warm reception in Australia, U.S. President Bill Clinton went for a moonlight boat ride on the waters of Sydney harbour on Wednesday night and prepared to meet "The Shark" -- Australian golf pro Greg Norman.

"I know this is called the Land Down Under, but after a day we all feel on top of the world," Clinton enthused at the start of a speech to the Australian parliament in Canberra earlier in the day, reflecting his delight at the friendliness he and his wife Hillary have encountered here.
"I have always wanted to come to Australia, but this has far exceeded my expectations," she told reporters travelling with the president.
The Clintons were the guests of Prime Minister John Howard for the harbour cruise, which showed off the dramatic Sydney skyline as they dined on salmon and Peking Duck.
A White House spokesman said the five-day visit was a tonic for the president and his wife after the rigours of the recent U.S. presidential election campaign.
It is largely a warm-up for an Asian trade summit in the Philippines next week, and Clinton used his speech to parliament to signal China that Washington is not bent on isolating the communist giant.
But at a luncheon in Clinton's honour, Australian opposition leader Kim Beazley warned him against all work and no play.
"Get out on the beaches. Get out on the golf courses. Get out snorkeling and have a terrific time here," Beazley urged.

On Thursday, Clinton planned to begin taking that advice in earnest. He had only one official event -- a speech to the people of Sydney in which he was to hold out the rich diversity of the United States and Australia as a model of tolerance and harmony for the world.
Afterwards, Clinton planned to live a duffer's dream by playing a round of golf with the legendary Greg Norman, also known as "The Shark".
Asked facetiously by a reporter how many strokes he would spot his opponent, Clinton replied: "No more than one a hole." Norman was in Sydney competing in the Australian Open golf tournament.

Clinton later planned to fly to Port Douglas in Australia's northern Queensland province, where the Great Barrier Reef is located. One of the world's most priceless natural resources, the Reef is teaming with marine life and is a world-renowned place for swimming and snorkeling.
